districtMeta.name: 48th Ward
districtMeta.description: The 48th Ward Civic Data Platform is a resident-focused resource for navigating local government, discovering neighborhood institutions, and participating in the decision-making process. Explore our community directory, track local legislation, and get involved in your ward.

officials.name: Leni Manaa-Hoppenworth
officials.title: 48th Ward Alderwoman
achievements: Zero pedestrian fatalities in the ward (2024–2026)
Secured $1.08M for 6 new Accessible Pedestrian Signals (APS)
Passed "ICE On Notice" Executive Order support (2026)
Bryn Mawr Historic District Landmark Status Initiative
officials.bio: Alderwoman Leni Manaa-Hoppenworth represents the 48th Ward on the Chicago City Council. She leads with a focus on transparency, community engagement, and data-driven governance, including the ward's innovative Participatory Budgeting program.

events.title: Ward Night with Alderwoman Leni
events.description: Join your neighbors to discuss zoning, development, housing, and infrastructure. Ward Nights occur on the 1st and 3rd Monday of each month.

events.title: Bryn Mawr Historic District Presentation
events.description: Preliminary landmark designation report presentation for the Bryn Mawr Historic District.

events.title: Street Sweeping Active
events.description: Chicago's street sweeping season is in full effect. Check your section schedule to avoid fines.

events.title: Spring Construction & Resurfacing
events.description: Annual street and alley resurfacing projects. Includes ADA ramp upgrades and utility work.

agencies.name: 48th Ward Office
agencies.description: The primary contact point for 48th Ward residents for city services, zoning, and neighborhood issues. Alderwoman Leni Manaa-Hoppenworth holds regular Ward Nights for constituent meetings.

agencies.name: Edgewater Chamber of Commerce
agencies.description: Supporting the growth and success of Edgewater businesses through advocacy, marketing, and networking. Manages the Edgewater Special Service Area.

agencies.name: Andersonville Chamber of Commerce
agencies.description: Promoting local and independent businesses in the Andersonville neighborhood. Produces the Midsommarfest and Andersonville Crawl events.

agencies.name: City of Chicago 311
agencies.description: Non-emergency city services platform for reporting issues and requesting services anywhere in Chicago.

agencies.name: Chicago Dept. of Buildings
agencies.description: Issues building permits and conducts inspections to ensure safe construction and code compliance across Chicago.

agencies.name: Chicago Dept. of Housing
agencies.description: Develops and preserves affordable housing, provides rental and homeownership assistance, and enforces tenant protections.

agencies.name: Chicago Dept. of Transportation (CDOT)
agencies.description: Plans and maintains Chicago's streets, sidewalks, traffic signals, and bike infrastructure. Key partner for ward pedestrian safety projects.

agencies.name: Chicago Transit Authority (CTA)
agencies.description: Operates the Red Line (Lawrence, Berwyn, Bryn Mawr, Thorndale, Granville stops serve the 48th Ward) plus bus routes including the 151, 136, and 147.

agencies.name: Chicago Public Schools (CPS)
agencies.description: Administers public K–12 education in Chicago, including Senn High School (IB World School) and multiple elementary schools serving 48th Ward families.

agencies.name: Chicago Park District
agencies.description: Manages Edgewater's lakefront parks, Berger Park, Margate Park, and Clarendon Park, providing recreation programming for all ages.

agencies.name: Chicago Dept. of Public Health (CDPH)
agencies.description: Provides disease surveillance, environmental health enforcement, and community health programs for Chicago residents.

agencies.name: Mayor's Office for People with Disabilities (MOPD)
agencies.description: Advocates for the rights and inclusion of Chicagoans with disabilities, providing services, resources, and ADA compliance enforcement.

agencies.name: Chicago City Clerk
agencies.description: Official record-keeper for the City of Chicago. Issues vehicle stickers, dog licenses, and business licenses, and maintains City Council documents.

agencies.name: City of Chicago Inspector General (OIG)
agencies.description: Independent watchdog that investigates fraud, waste, abuse, and misconduct by City employees and contractors.

agencies.name: Chicago Fire Department
agencies.description: Provides emergency fire suppression, emergency medical services, and fire prevention programs. Engine 78 and Truck 14 serve the 48th Ward area.

agencies.name: Chicago Police — 20th District (Rogers Park)
agencies.description: The 20th Police District (Lakeview/Edgewater) serves the 48th Ward. Hosts CAPS (Community Alternative Policing Strategy) beat meetings.

agencies.name: Cook County Assessor
agencies.description: Determines the assessed value of all properties in Cook County for property tax purposes. Administers homeowner, senior, and disability exemptions.

agencies.name: Cook County Clerk (Elections)
agencies.description: Administers elections, voter registration, and early voting for Cook County residents outside the City of Chicago. Also maintains vital records (birth, death, marriage certificates).

agencies.name: Cook County Sheriff
agencies.description: Provides law enforcement for unincorporated Cook County and operates the Cook County Jail. Also serves civil court orders throughout the county.

agencies.name: Cook County Health — John H. Stroger Jr. Hospital
agencies.description: The county's flagship public hospital providing comprehensive care regardless of ability to pay. The CountyCare Medicaid managed care plan is administered here.

agencies.name: Cook County Legal Aid for Housing & Debt
agencies.description: Provides free legal assistance to low-income Cook County residents facing eviction, foreclosure, or debt collection.

agencies.name: Cook County Commissioner — 8th District
agencies.description: The Cook County Board of Commissioners sets the county budget and policy. The 8th District includes much of the 48th Ward area.

agencies.name: Illinois Secretary of State
agencies.description: Handles driver's licenses, vehicle registration, business entity filings, and administers the state library system.

agencies.name: Illinois Dept. of Employment Security (IDES)
agencies.description: Administers unemployment insurance benefits and workforce development programs for Illinois workers.

agencies.name: Illinois Dept. of Human Services (IDHS)
agencies.description: Administers SNAP, cash assistance, child care, and community-based social services for Illinois families in need.

agencies.name: Illinois Healthcare & Family Services (HFS) — Medicaid
agencies.description: Administers the Illinois Medicaid program (All Kids, FamilyCare, ACA Marketplace) and Child Support Services.

agencies.name: Illinois Dept. on Aging
agencies.description: Funds and coordinates community-based services that help older Illinoisans live independently, including the CIL network and senior centers.

agencies.name: Illinois Dept. of Children & Family Services (DCFS)
agencies.description: Investigates child abuse and neglect, provides foster care and adoption services, and funds community-based child welfare programs.

agencies.name: Illinois Housing Development Authority (IHDA)
agencies.description: Finances affordable housing development and provides down payment assistance programs for first-time homebuyers across Illinois.
agencies.address: 111 E Wacker Dr, Suite 1000, Chicago, IL 60601

agencies.name: Illinois Environmental Protection Agency (IEPA)
agencies.description: Regulates air, water, and land environmental quality in Illinois. Handles pollution complaints and administers cleanup programs.

agencies.name: Illinois Dept. of Transportation (IDOT)
agencies.description: Plans and maintains Illinois state highways, bridges, and transit systems, including I-94 (Edens) and US-41 (Lake Shore Drive) near the ward.

agencies.name: Illinois Attorney General
agencies.description: Enforces state law, protects consumers from fraud, and provides victim services. Operates a consumer complaint hotline.

agencies.name: Illinois State Board of Elections
agencies.description: Administers state and federal election law, oversees candidate filing, and maintains the statewide voter registration database.

agencies.name: Illinois Legal Aid Online (ILAO)
agencies.description: Free online resource connecting Illinois residents to legal information, self-help forms, and referrals to legal aid organizations.

agencies.name: Illinois Commerce Commission (ICC)
agencies.description: Regulates electric, natural gas, and telecommunications utilities operating in Illinois. Handles consumer utility complaints.

agencies.name: Illinois Dept. of Financial & Professional Regulation (IDFPR)
agencies.description: Licenses and regulates over 1 million professionals in Illinois, including healthcare workers, real estate agents, and financial institutions.

agencies.name: Illinois Lt. Governor — Community Programs Office
agencies.description: The Lt. Governor's office administers community grants, rural affairs, and coordinates state outreach to local communities.

agencies.name: U.S. Senator Dick Durbin — Chicago Office
agencies.description: Senator Durbin's Chicago constituent services office assists Illinois residents with federal agency issues including immigration, Social Security, VA, and passports.
agencies.address: 230 S Dearborn St, Suite 3892, Chicago, IL 60604

agencies.name: U.S. Senator Tammy Duckworth — Chicago Office
agencies.description: Senator Duckworth's Chicago office helps Illinois residents navigate federal programs and provides constituent services for veterans, seniors, and families.
agencies.address: 230 S Dearborn St, Suite 3900, Chicago, IL 60604

agencies.name: U.S. Rep. Jan Schakowsky — 9th District (Evanston Office)
agencies.description: Rep. Schakowsky's district office serves 48th Ward residents with federal casework. Evanston office covers the North Shore and Edgewater area.

agencies.name: Social Security Administration — Rogers Park Field Office
agencies.description: Administers Social Security retirement, disability (SSDI), and Supplemental Security Income (SSI) programs. The closest field office to the 48th Ward.

agencies.name: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS)
agencies.description: Federal agency overseeing Medicare health coverage for people 65+ and certain disabled individuals. Use 1-800-MEDICARE or medicare.gov for enrollment.

agencies.name: U.S. Dept. of Housing & Urban Development (HUD) — Chicago Regional Office
agencies.description: Federal housing agency providing community development grants, fair housing enforcement, and Section 8 voucher program oversight.

agencies.name: Jesse Brown VA Medical Center
agencies.description: The VA medical center serving Chicago-area veterans with full inpatient, outpatient, and mental health services. Clinics and CBOCs serve North Side veterans.

agencies.name: U.S. Small Business Administration (SBA) — Illinois District
agencies.description: Provides small business loans, grants, counseling, and government contracting assistance. Serves Edgewater and Andersonville small business owners.
agencies.address: 500 W Madison St, Suite 1150, Chicago, IL 60661

agencies.name: U.S. Dept. of Labor — Chicago Regional Office
agencies.description: Enforces federal workplace laws including wage and hour, workplace safety (OSHA), and employee benefits (ERISA) protections.
agencies.address: 230 S Dearborn St, Room 774, Chicago, IL 60604

agencies.name: IRS Taxpayer Assistance Center — Chicago
agencies.description: Provides in-person federal tax help. Appointment required. Referrals available to VITA (Volunteer Income Tax Assistance) free tax prep sites.

agencies.name: U.S. Citizenship & Immigration Services (USCIS) — Chicago Field Office
agencies.description: Processes immigration applications for permanent residence, naturalization, asylum, and work authorization for Chicago-area applicants.

agencies.name: FEMA Region 5 — Chicago
agencies.description: Coordinates federal disaster response and preparedness for Illinois and the Great Lakes region. Manages flood insurance and disaster relief.

agencies.name: U.S. Post Office — Edgewater Station
agencies.description: Provides postal services for the Edgewater and Andersonville area, including mail delivery, PO boxes, and passport photo services.

agencies.name: Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC) — Chicago District
agencies.description: Enforces federal laws prohibiting employment discrimination based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, disability, or genetic information.
agencies.address: 230 S Dearborn St, Suite 2920, Chicago, IL 60604

civicGroups.name: 48th Ward Democrats
civicGroups.focus: Local Democratic Party ward organization for Edgewater & Andersonville
civicGroups.description: The official Democratic Party ward organization for the 48th Ward. Organizes voter outreach, candidate endorsements, and local political education for ward precincts.

civicGroups.name: Edgewater Neighborhood Association (ENA)
civicGroups.focus: Civic advocacy and community improvement for the Edgewater neighborhood
civicGroups.description: The Edgewater Neighborhood Association advocates for residents on issues including land use, public safety, housing, and quality of life. Holds regular community meetings open to all residents.

civicGroups.name: ONE Northside
civicGroups.focus: Progressive community organizing on housing, education, and immigrant rights on the North Side
civicGroups.description: ONE Northside is a broad-based community organization building power across North Side neighborhoods. It leads campaigns for affordable housing, school equity, and immigrant rights through door-knocking and direct action.

civicGroups.name: Northside Community Development Corporation
civicGroups.focus: Affordable housing development and economic opportunity on Chicago's North Side
civicGroups.description: Northside CDC develops and preserves affordable rental housing and provides homeownership counseling and financial literacy resources for low-to-moderate income North Side residents.

civicGroups.name: Howard Brown Health
civicGroups.focus: LGBTQ+-affirming healthcare for Chicagoans, with major presence in Andersonville
civicGroups.description: Howard Brown Health is a Federally Qualified Health Center providing primary care, behavioral health, HIV/STI services, and pharmacy to LGBTQ+ people and allies. The Brown Elephant thrift stores fund their mission.

civicGroups.name: Heartland Alliance / Heartland Human Care Services
civicGroups.focus: Anti-poverty services including housing, healthcare, and economic opportunity for the most vulnerable
civicGroups.description: Heartland Alliance and its affiliate Heartland Human Care Services provide housing, mental health, refugee resettlement, and workforce services to people experiencing poverty, homelessness, or displacement.

civicGroups.name: Thresholds
civicGroups.focus: Mental health advocacy and community-based treatment for people with serious mental illness
civicGroups.description: Thresholds provides comprehensive mental health and substance use services, supportive housing, and employment programs across Chicago, including offices serving North Side residents.

civicGroups.name: Asian Human Services
civicGroups.focus: Comprehensive social, health, and educational services for Chicago's diverse Asian communities
civicGroups.description: Asian Human Services provides multilingual social services, mental health counseling, early childhood education, and elder services for the diverse Asian immigrant communities throughout Edgewater and the broader North Side.

civicGroups.name: Swedish American Museum
civicGroups.focus: Preserving and celebrating Swedish and Scandinavian-American heritage in Andersonville
civicGroups.description: The Swedish American Museum is Andersonville's cultural anchor, housing permanent and rotating exhibits on Swedish immigration history, the Nordic Room children's museum, and hosting community cultural events.

civicGroups.name: Edgewater Historical Society
civicGroups.focus: Documenting and preserving the history of the Edgewater neighborhood
civicGroups.description: The Edgewater Historical Society collects, preserves, and shares the history of the Edgewater community through exhibits, archives, walking tours, and public programs.

civicGroups.name: Lawrence Hall Youth Services
civicGroups.focus: Trauma-informed care and residential services for at-risk youth and young adults
civicGroups.description: Lawrence Hall provides foster care, residential treatment, community-based family services, and transitional living programs for youth who have experienced trauma, abuse, or neglect in the Chicago area.

civicGroups.name: Lakewood-Balmoral Residents Council
civicGroups.focus: Preserving the historic character and residential quality of the Lakewood-Balmoral neighborhood
civicGroups.description: The Lakewood-Balmoral Residents Council advocates for the historic, tree-lined Lakewood-Balmoral district within the 48th Ward, engaging on zoning, preservation, and neighborhood beautification.

civicGroups.name: Bryn Mawr Improvement Association
civicGroups.focus: Advocating for beautification and historic preservation along the Bryn Mawr corridor
civicGroups.description: The Bryn Mawr Improvement Association works to enhance the Bryn Mawr Historic District, supporting landmarking efforts, storefront improvements, and neighborhood events.

civicGroups.name: Loyola University — Center for Experiential Learning
civicGroups.focus: Connecting Loyola University students with community service and civic engagement opportunities on the North Side
civicGroups.description: Loyola's Center for Experiential Learning places students in service-learning roles and community partnerships across Edgewater, Rogers Park, and the broader North Side, supporting nonprofits and local initiatives.

civicGroups.name: Chicago DSA — North Side Branch
civicGroups.focus: Democratic socialist organizing on housing, labor, and social justice on Chicago's North Side
civicGroups.description: The North Side Branch of Chicago Democratic Socialists of America organizes around tenant rights, labor issues, and electoral politics, with significant membership in Edgewater and Andersonville.

civicGroups.name: Pride in Edgewater
civicGroups.focus: LGBTQ+ community visibility, advocacy, and celebration in the Edgewater neighborhood
civicGroups.description: Pride in Edgewater organizes LGBTQ+ community events, advocates for inclusive policies, and builds connections between LGBTQ+ residents and local institutions in the neighborhood.

civicGroups.name: Edgewater Garden Club
civicGroups.focus: Community greening, parkway planting, and beautification across Edgewater
civicGroups.description: The Edgewater Garden Club organizes neighborhood beautification through parkway gardens, community planters, and green-thumb programming, working with residents and the Park District.

civicGroups.name: CAPS Beat 1913 — Edgewater West
civicGroups.focus: Community policing partnership for Beat 1913 covering western Edgewater
civicGroups.description: CAPS (Chicago Alternative Policing Strategy) Beat 1913 brings together residents and police for monthly beat meetings to address local crime concerns and build community safety.

civicGroups.name: CAPS Beat 1914 — Edgewater East / Lakefront
civicGroups.focus: Community policing partnership for Beat 1914 covering eastern Edgewater and the lakefront
civicGroups.description: CAPS Beat 1914 facilitates regular community-police dialogue for the lakefront Edgewater area, addressing quality-of-life issues and promoting neighbor-to-neighbor safety strategies.

civicGroups.name: CAPS Beat 1912 — Andersonville / Clark St Corridor
civicGroups.focus: Community policing partnership for Beat 1912 in the Andersonville and Clark St area
civicGroups.description: CAPS Beat 1912 serves the Andersonville commercial corridor and surrounding residential blocks, coordinating between business owners, residents, and local police on safety concerns.

civicGroups.name: Broadway/Clark Corridor Business Alliance
civicGroups.focus: Supporting small business vitality along the Broadway and Clark Street corridors
civicGroups.description: A collaborative of small business owners and property stakeholders along the Broadway and Clark corridors advocating for corridor improvements, vacancy reduction, and supportive zoning.

civicGroups.name: Chicago Filmmakers
civicGroups.focus: Supporting independent filmmakers through screenings, education, and artist services in Edgewater
civicGroups.description: Chicago Filmmakers provides production resources, filmmaker education, and community film screenings. Their Edgewater home is a hub for independent cinema on the North Side.

civicGroups.name: Raven Theatre Company
civicGroups.focus: Professional live theater rooted in the Edgewater community
civicGroups.description: Raven Theatre is one of Chicago's premier storefront theater companies, producing professional productions in Edgewater and offering education programs for youth and adults.

civicGroups.name: Chicago Recovery Alliance (CRA)
civicGroups.focus: Harm reduction services for people who use drugs, including needle exchange and naloxone distribution
civicGroups.description: Chicago Recovery Alliance provides harm reduction services including needle/syringe exchange, naloxone (Narcan) distribution, and drug-user health education with mobile outreach across Chicago neighborhoods.

civicGroups.name: Edgewater / Uptown Arts Center Collaborative
civicGroups.focus: Connecting arts organizations and residents to celebrate the cultural diversity of Edgewater and Uptown
civicGroups.description: A coalition of arts organizations working across the Edgewater-Uptown border to produce community arts events, mural projects, and public space activation reflecting the neighborhoods' diverse communities.

legislation.title: ICE On Notice Executive Order (EO 2026-1)
legislation.summary: Directs CPD to investigate and document alleged illegal activity by federal immigration agents to protect Chicago residents.
legislation.impact: Protects immigrant communities and increases oversight of federal agents.

legislation.title: Broadway Corridor Upzoning
legislation.summary: Legislative effort to simplify zoning along Broadway to encourage small business density and affordable housing near Red Line stations.
legislation.impact: Economic growth and increased housing density near transit.

legislation.title: Accessible Pedestrian Signals Initiative
legislation.summary: Allocation of $1.08M for 6 new APS signals at key ward intersections including Sheridan & Balmoral and Broadway & Argyle.
legislation.impact: Increased safety and accessibility for residents with disabilities.

benefits.title: Participatory Budgeting Voting
benefits.description: Vote on how to spend $1,000,000 of the ward's infrastructure budget.
benefits.howToApply: Vote online or in-person during the annual spring cycle.

benefits.title: Homeowner Property Tax Exemptions
benefits.description: Various exemptions available for homeowners, seniors, and veterans to reduce property tax bills.
benefits.howToApply: Apply via the Cook County Assessor's website.
